subject.measured_quantity: provider-reported token usage of an AI agent completing an accepted equivalent repository task
subject.interpretation: AIT and Git do not intrinsically consume model tokens; this protocol compares declared agent workflow surfaces.

executors.axis: executor is a pinned campaign axis; one campaign runs exactly one executor, and cross-executor results are reported side by side under their own campaigns, never pooled or paired
executors.shared_permission_scope: both executors declare the identical ait_benchmark_local_v1 filesystem scope recorded in the per-run codex-permission-profile.json artifact (legacy shared filename); Codex enforces it through its native permission profile, Claude through the workspace working directory, --add-dir roots, and the pinned tool allow/deny lists

codex.rejected_apply_patch_authority: rejected apply_patch attempts recorded by Codex stderr
codex.infrastructure_failure_signals: structured error events, turn.failed, error items, and candidate tool-process spawn failures

claude.program: claude CLI headless: --print --output-format stream-json --verbose --no-session-persistence --strict-mcp-config --setting-sources "" (zero settings-file contamination), --settings with the inline sandbox policy, --tools pinning the exact built-in tool availability surface; model fallbacks disabled
claude.usage_authority: the single terminal result event; normalized input_tokens = direct input plus cache_read plus cache_creation tokens so cached input remains a subset of input and provider_total = input plus output
claude.feature_overrides: exactly the declared allowed-tool and disallowed-tool lists, recorded verbatim as the campaign feature-override evidence
claude.completed_file_change_authority: Edit or Write tool_use events whose tool_result completed without is_error
claude.rejected_apply_patch_authority: Edit or Write tool_use events whose tool_result reports is_error
claude.infrastructure_failure_signals: a terminal result event with a non-success subtype or is_error, structured stream error events, or a session that ends without any terminal result event
claude.network_enforcement: bash sandbox enabled in strict mode (unsandboxed-command escape hatch disabled) with external network egress denied at the sandbox proxy and loopback binding allowed, matching disabled_except_loopback; verified by probe: external curl blocked, 127.0.0.1 listen permitted
claude.tool_surface_enforcement: availability pinned with --tools to exactly the allowed set, and the transcript validator fails the lane closed on any tool_use event outside that set
claude.filesystem_enforcement: sandbox filesystem writes scoped to the lane working directory plus exactly the declared additional workspace roots and Git write exceptions via sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite; verified by probe outside the tmp default-allow zone: listed roots writable including nested directory creation, unlisted external paths denied

core.topology: one fresh single-agent session per run

modes.repository_surface: real local Git main worktree plus one measured linked task worktree, without .ait metadata
modes.required_evidence: task-relevant explicit Git discovery plus exactly one linked-worktree creation, final candidate commit, fast-forward integration onto main, linked-worktree removal, and temporary-branch deletion
modes.metadata_isolation: each run owns a writable external Git directory connected to its fresh main worktree through a standard .git gitfile, plus one task path below an otherwise empty benchmark-owned writable worktree container; the narrow no-network shared executor permission scope reopens only the current run's protected Git pointer and resolved metadata, and no inherited GIT_DIR or GIT_WORK_TREE override is used

modes.repository_surface: current solo_local sprint-off AIT Task, Snapshot, and local Task-finish workflow
modes.required_evidence: runner-admitted solo_local sprint-off authority plus measured task start, task finish, and task-relevant local AIT workflow commands

mode.repository_surface: one fresh AIT linear session with one benchmark-owned compact execution brief
mode.claim_boundary: benchmark context experiment; it does not change the current AIT product workflow

brief_constraints: derived from the shared task contract
contains no solution or file-location hint absent from shared inputs
generation cost is counted in first-use or precomputed symmetrically in steady-state

first_use_total_cost.repository_identity_policy: both modes pin benchmark-agent identity inside the fresh repository before the baseline revision

workloads.name: projectile-cooldown-regression
workloads.required_outcome: diagnose and repair a seeded rapid-fire or cooldown defect without unrelated gameplay changes

workloads.name: armored-enemy-feature
workloads.required_outcome: add a deterministic two-hit enemy, score rule, original visual distinction, and tests

workloads.name: replay-divergence-diagnosis
workloads.required_outcome: repair seeded replay divergence after pause and resume

workloads.name: gameplay-modularization
workloads.required_outcome: split a monolithic gameplay implementation while preserving exact observable behavior

workloads.name: beta-release-hardening
workloads.required_outcome: add replay persistence, settings schema, mobile input, focus recovery, benchmark UI, validation, and release documentation

fixture_contract.tracked_content_equivalence: byte-equivalent content digest for every paired mode in one comparison cell
required_properties: original local HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and assets
no backend or external network dependency
machine-readable input, event-log, observable-state, startup, and validation contracts

provider_usage.authority: provider-reported machine-readable session log or API response
provider_usage.provider_session_failure_policy: retain a lane with any structured provider error event as infrastructure-invalid even when later commands, usage, or exit status appear successful
provider_usage.candidate_tool_process_spawn_failure_pol: retain the invalid run and stop the remaining schedule immediately even when the model recovers and exits zero; recognize both unified CreateProcess stderr and non-unified executor Io/exit-code-minus-one evidence

executor_preflight.topology: one fresh ephemeral session of the pinned campaign executor in an isolated temporary directory
executor_preflight.model_and_runtime_pin: exact campaign executor executable, model id and revision, reasoning effort, the shared ait_benchmark_local_v1 permission scope (Codex extends :workspace natively; Claude enforces the identical scope through its pinned tool policy), disabled command network, project-document limit, and default feature settings
git_worktree_permission_probe_commands: git worktree add on a temporary branch
git commit --allow-empty in the linked worktree
executor_preflight.git_worktree_permission_probe_accounting: runner admission without a model request; completes through the exact generated shared permission profile before the 30-command model executor probe and every candidate lane
executor_preflight.command_lifecycle_order: each command item must complete before the next command item starts
executor_preflight.token_accounting: record separately as admission overhead; never include in AIT or Git metrics
executor_preflight.failure_policy: preserve create-new preflight evidence, start zero candidate lanes, emit a stopped execution result, and require a new campaign identity after runtime recovery

primary_metrics.effective_tokens_per_accepted_task: sum(provider_total_tokens for every valid attempted run) / count(accepted equivalent outcomes)

mixed_workflow_metrics.pair_admission: exact common workload_id plus attempt with two protocol-valid summaries and normalized provider usage; workflow metric asymmetry never excludes the pair
mixed_workflow_metrics.reduction_formula: 100 * (1 - AIT / Git) when the Git baseline is positive
mixed_workflow_metrics.zero_git_baseline_encoding: null reduction with both raw mode values retained

fairness.project_document_loading: disabled symmetrically with project_doc_max_bytes=0; mode rules come only from the frozen measured prompt
fairness.measured_ait_treatment: accounting-profile-specific prose; steady-state contains only one local task start, returned worktree entry, project editing and validation, optional intermediate Snapshot, and one local task finish; every Git command is explicitly prohibited while read-only AIT inspection (status, diff, blame) is informational and unrestricted, symmetric with the Git treatment's unrestricted status, diff, and log inspection; environment admission is runner-owned outside model accounting
measured_ait_allowed_commands: read-only help introspection of the mode's own CLI (--help, -h, or a leading help subcommand): informational, exempt from lifecycle counts and surface checks, token cost measured; cross-tool help remains prohibited
read-only local inspection with ait status, ait diff, or ait blame: informational, exempt from lifecycle counts and surface checks, token cost measured; any remote authority remains prohibited

informational_cli_help_introspection.allowed: the mode's own repository CLI only, symmetrically for both executors
informational_cli_help_introspection.accounting: token cost stays in the measurement; the invocation is not a lifecycle step
informational_cli_help_introspection.cross_tool_policy: help of the other mode's CLI remains a mode-exclusion violation

symmetric_readonly_inspection.rationale: each measured mode must reach repository state through its own native read-only channel; denying one side that channel forces its verification demand into full project validation runs and inflates its measured cost, which observation at high reasoning effort confirmed
symmetric_readonly_inspection.accounting: token cost stays in the measurement; the invocation is not a lifecycle step and not a forbidden surface
symmetric_readonly_inspection.remote_authority_policy: never informational: any remote-carrying inspection remains a mode violation
symmetric_readonly_inspection.management_surface_policy: unchanged: task list, change list, task audit, queue summary, plan, workflow, and remote surfaces remain forbidden
symmetric_readonly_inspection.prior_revision_note: revisions through game-development-2026-08-25.24 measured the AIT mode without an inspection channel while instructing project-local validation as the substitute; the codex r14 and r15 columns were measured under that prior asymmetric wording

fairness.measured_git_treatment: accounting-profile-specific prose; steady-state starts from a runner-bootstrapped worktree with a recorded proof that symbolic HEAD is clean main and equals refs/heads/main, then the measured agent creates one benchmark-task linked worktree from either explicit main or the proven current HEAD, edits and validates only there, creates one candidate commit, fast-forwards main, removes the linked worktree, and deletes the temporary branch; first-use has no runner-owned start proof and still requires explicit main; every AIT command is explicitly prohibited
fairness.cross_mode_repository_command_exclusion: mutually exclusive and fail-closed: AIT treatment prohibits every Git command, and Git treatment prohibits every AIT command
measured_git_required_commands: steady-state: git worktree add -b benchmark-task <benchmark-owned-path> main, or omit main only with the runner-owned clean-main HEAD proof
first-use: git worktree add -b benchmark-task <benchmark-owned-path> main
git commit (exactly one final candidate commit in steady state)

git_worktree_start_point_admission.explicit_main: always admitted when the remaining declared worktree lifecycle matches
git_worktree_start_point_admission.implicit_head: admitted only in steady-state when git-start-state-proof.json was captured before the provider turn and proves an empty porcelain status, symbolic main, and HEAD equal to refs/heads/main; the declared worktree path must be the final positional argument, so no alternate commit-ish is present; closeout must additionally prove that ORIG_HEAD and the candidate commit parent both equal the recorded start HEAD
git_worktree_start_point_admission.first_use: implicit HEAD is rejected because repository creation occurs inside the measured provider turn and no runner-owned start proof exists
git_worktree_start_point_admission.predecessor_evidence: protocol .27 continuation retains its frozen proof-backed implicit-main treatment; protocol .26 retains its frozen literal-main classification and is never reinterpreted by this successor rule

fairness.git_metadata_layout: normal per-run separate Git directory connected through a standard .git gitfile; the metadata directory and an empty worktree container are additional roots of the ait_benchmark_local_v1 profile, while exact write exceptions reopen only the main .git pointer, resolved metadata, and task-worktree .git pointer; the task child is deletable without exposing sibling evidence and commands discover metadata after cd without inherited GIT_DIR or GIT_WORK_TREE
fairness.git_metadata_override_admission: reject GIT_DIR or GIT_WORK_TREE assignments applied to Git, persistent shell exports of either variable, and global git --git-dir/--work-tree options before the subcommand; admit read-only subcommand query options such as git rev-parse --git-dir

permission_profile.name: ait_benchmark_local_v1
permission_profile.git_write_exception_scope: current run main .git pointer, resolved external metadata, and linked-task .git pointer only
permission_profile.executor_enforcement: Codex enforces the profile natively; Claude enforces the identical declared scope through workspace working directory, --add-dir roots, and the pinned tool allow/deny lists

complete_campaign.revision_note: .29 retains the exact .27 prompts, fixtures, evaluator, symmetric read-only inspection treatment, proof-backed implicit-main treatment, and twenty-pair 200-session sampling authority; it adds only the narrow repository-owner-authorized transparent statistical replacement policy for the named GD-05 AIT lane after .28 completed the frozen schedule without retry

sampling.aggregate_method: median of paired workload and run ratios

atomic_pair_schedule.pair_order: randomize workload pairs inside each block, then randomize Git/AIT order inside each adjacent pair
atomic_pair_schedule.slice_unit: --max-pairs counts complete adjacent Git/AIT pairs; --max-runs is retired
atomic_pair_schedule.candidate_defect_policy: retain a protocol-valid unaccepted candidate as a measured outcome, finish the counterpart when safe, and continue the exact suffix without retry; an invalid attempt stops after its completed pair and an infrastructure failure stops immediately

immutable_resume.scope: a stopped .27 complete campaign may resume under the .28 controller when its existing run IDs are an exact protocol-valid complete-pair prefix of its frozen schedule; legacy .20 retains only its existing narrow .21-adjudicator path; all other predecessors are read-only
immutable_resume.existing_run_policy: never recreate, overwrite, or retry an existing run ID; execute only the missing schedule suffix with identical pinned tool versions
immutable_resume.valid_unaccepted_outcome_policy: retain every valid unaccepted prefix run as measured evidence and continue only the missing suffix; it remains acceptance-penalized and cannot be repaired, replaced, or retried
immutable_resume.validator_adjudication_policy: append-only and digest-linked to the immutable raw summary and transcript; limited to the exact read-only git rev-parse --git-dir false positive; no measured field may change
immutable_resume.derived_report_policy: archive each replaced derived report by content digest before atomically publishing the refreshed effective view
immutable_resume.resume_audit_policy: record each resume start and result append-only under a monotonically numbered resumptions directory with source and controller protocol revisions, continuation policy, runner path, and runner SHA-256

statistical_replacement.execution_limit: exactly one new AIT session; no second replacement or repair is admitted
statistical_replacement.pin_equivalence: campaign manifest, fixture manifest, prompt bytes, model and reasoning pin, executor and tool versions, permission and network policy, cache class, run identity axes, initial content digest, and executor preflight must match the disclosed source lane
statistical_replacement.admission: the replacement must be protocol-valid, evaluator-accepted, browser-passed, workflow-closed, and carry valid transcript and normalized provider usage
statistical_replacement.history: retain the original valid functional failure and every raw artifact append-only; record source and replacement run-summary digests plus replacement-runner digest in statistical-replacement.json
statistical_replacement.statistical_view: exclude only the named source AIT lane, admit only the named replacement AIT lane against the unchanged Git counterpart, and calculate effective statistics over exactly 200 admitted sessions from 201 executed evidence sessions
statistical_replacement.claim_policy: source_protocol_claim_eligible remains false; effective claim_eligible may be true only when the replacement-qualified 200-session matrix has no claim blockers and positive primary statistics
statistical_replacement.disclosure: publish the excluded failure, reason, exact replacement mapping, executed and admitted counts, and checksummed provenance

paired_comparison_admission.admit_when: both Git and AIT lanes share the exact workload plus attempt identity, are protocol-valid, and carry normalized provider usage
paired_comparison_admission.workflow_metric_asymmetry_policy: retain the pair and report the difference
paired_comparison_admission.completed_file_change_authority: the pinned executor's completed-file-change authority declared in the executors section
paired_comparison_admission.rejected_apply_patch_authority: the pinned executor's rejected-apply-patch authority declared in the executors section
paired_comparison_admission.total_patch_attempt_authority: completed file-change items plus rejected apply-patch attempts under the pinned executor's authorities

Git mode invoked any AIT command

publication_provenance.source_claim_eligibility_policy: evaluate under the declared source protocol without relabeling its campaign scope
publication_provenance.predecessor_complete_campaign_policy: .22 through .25 complete evidence remains readable only at its original ten-pair-per-workload, 100-session shape; .26 remains read-only at its original twenty-pair-per-workload, 200-session shape and literal-main classifications; .27 remains frozen at its original twenty-pair-per-workload, 200-session shape and proof-backed implicit-main classifications and is narrowly resumable only under the provenance-recorded .28 controller; .29 may derive only the explicitly authorized transparent statistical view while preserving .27 source-protocol status and all 201 raw sessions; predecessors are never reinterpreted as current .29 source evidence
publication_provenance.legacy_pilot_policy: pilot evidence remains pilot and is never source-protocol claim eligible
publication_provenance.current_policy_reanalysis: report separately as retrospective criteria satisfaction; it never changes source scope or source-protocol claim eligibility
publication_provenance.replacement_qualified_publication_policy: the exact .29 replacement-qualified statistical view may publish claim_eligible=true while separately retaining source_protocol_claim_eligible=false, the original failure, its exclusion, the replacement, and all provenance digests
publication_provenance.descriptive_publication_policy: fully disclosed pilot measurements may be published as pilot results but not as original-protocol-qualified claims

publication_eligibility.scope: game-development workloads, pinned model, declared profile, and declared topology only

non_goals: claim AIT always uses fewer tokens than Git
claim AIT is faster or cheaper for every repository task
compare different model providers inside one AIT-versus-Git claim
generalize game-development results to unrelated domains
treat token savings alone as developer productivity
